note: Second variant, same design. Make the crab shell a muted GREY-BLUE slate (#6A8BBB, clearly greyer and less saturated than cornflower or royal blue). Hold the big hammer claw a little higher and more forward so all four walking legs are fully visible below it, none hidden behind the claw arm. Keep the stern face, the dark basalt boulder, barnacles, coral-pink patches, seaweed tuft and coral-pink antennae.

Third variant, same design. Crab shell muted GREY-BLUE slate (#6A8BBB). FACE FIX: under the head plate the face is ONE simple pale sea-foam aqua area with only the small slightly-open mouth in it (deep rose inside) and two tiny rounded mouth flaps beside the mouth: NO dark holes, NO fangs, NO dark shapes that could look like a second pair of eyes. The only eyes are the two amber eyes on the stalks. Big hammer claw held forward so all four walking legs stay fully visible; the legs come out from under the crab's front body and the boulder opening, spread apart.
